summary: Redis is persistently configured and running on node1. The dedicated inventory ACL identity works, its generated credential is stored at /etc/redis-inventory.env with root:root 0600 permissions, and service/data recovery was proven after one full node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed Arch Linux’s official Redis-compatible provider, Valkey 9.1.2, including redis-server, redis-cli, and redis.service compatibility.
Enabled AOF persistence with every-second fsync under /var/lib/valkey.
Created the inventory ACL identity, restricted it to inventory:* keys, and disabled unauthenticated default-user access.
Generated a 64-character credential on node1 and stored it in /etc/redis-inventory.env.
Enabled the service and verified it on node1’s managed IP.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified its changed boot identity, service recovery, authentication, ACL enforcement, and persisted data.

evidence.summary: Arch’s package metadata identifies Valkey as the Redis provider; compatibility binaries and redis.service exist, and the post-reboot service is active and listening on 10.100.11.10:6379.
AOF is configured with every-second fsync; live status reports successful writes, non-empty AOF files exist, and inventory:persistence-proof retained its value after node reboot.
The inventory ACL is defined and authenticates as inventory; anonymous access and writes outside inventory:* are denied both before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Generated credential stored with root-only access
evidence.summary: The node-generated credential is 64 characters long and /etc/redis-inventory.env remains root:root mode 0600 after reboot; no credential value was exposed.

The healthy baseline used boot ID 1db3db2e-dca8-44d6-8402-3b99605ae056; the reboot was acknowledged before disconnect; the recovered node reported boot ID 8018c0c9-ad0e-4b7a-81f3-a24540a0282b; Redis, its listener, inventory authentication, AOF status, credential permissions, and persisted data all recovered.
